title: Reporting Bargaining Shifts in Mediation Minutes

sections.content: You know the *imperfecto* from A2 Unit 21, the *condicional* from A2 Unit 26, the *pluscuamperfecto* from B1 Unit 1, basic reported speech (*decir*, *afirmar*, *declarar* + backshifted tenses) from B1 Unit 13, and *advertir* from B2 Unit 18. In formal mediation minutes (*actas de mediación*), verbs such as *sostener* ('to maintain'), *advertir* ('to warn'), *aclarar* ('to clarify') and *anunciar* trace how each delegation's offer evolved across rounds. When reporting an expired round or past condition, tenses shift back regularly (present → imperfect, preterite/present perfect → pluperfect, future → conditional). However, when a past reporting verb introduces an offer or deadline that remains open at the time of reporting, the subordinate verb can stay in the present or future indicative to signal that the commitment is still active on the table.

sections.title: Backshifted Rounds vs Still-Open Offers
rows: Prior action before the session (pluperfect *había* + participle)
La dirección sostuvo que ya había desbloqueado el presupuesto. (Management maintained that it had already unlocked the budget.)
El comité advirtió que no aceptaría otro ultimátum. (The committee warned that it would not accept another ultimatum.)
El mediador declaró que las conversaciones se estancaban. (The mediator stated that the talks were stalling.)
Offer still valid right now (no backshift: present / future)
La portavoz aclaró ayer que la moratoria sigue vigente hoy. (The spokesperson clarified yesterday that the moratorium remains in force today.)

items.spanish: El delegado afirmó que el desacuerdo había provocado un punto muerto.
items.english: The delegate stated that the disagreement had caused a deadlock.

items.spanish: La empresa anunció que renegociaría los plazos tras la moratoria.
items.english: The company announced that it would renegotiate the deadlines after the moratorium.

items.spanish: La mediadora advirtió que un ultimátum no desbloquearía la sesión.
items.english: The mediator warned that an ultimatum would not unlock the session.

items.spanish: El acta recogió ayer que las dos partes renegociarán la tarifa el jueves.
items.english: The minutes recorded yesterday that both sides will renegotiate the rate on Thursday.

sections.content: Look at the time anchor before choosing the tense after a past reporting verb. With a closed past anchor (*en la ronda anterior*, *aquel martes*), shift back to the imperfect, pluperfect or conditional. With an anchor that is still current (*hoy*, *todavía hoy*, *el próximo jueves*), the present or future is fully grammatical.
